Both disclosures describe the remarketing of specific unsecured general obligation bonds issued by the Industrial Development Authority of the City of Chandler, Arizona (and/or State of Oregon). The 2023 disclosure notes the remarketing of $423 million in bonds maturing in 2035/2040 with specific coupons. The 2024 disclosure notes the remarketing of $438 million of Arizona bonds maturing in 2049 with a 4.0% coupon. Both refer to the same specific facility/authority bonds being remarketed in the respective years, maintaining the same specific subject matter (Arizona/Oregon bonds remarketing).

comparisons.peer_topic: Issuance and Terms of Senior Notes
comparisons.peer_summary: On June 9, 2022, the Company issued $1.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of 3.924% Senior Notes Due 2032 and 4.393% Senior Notes Due 2052, which are general unsecured senior obligations governed by a June 9, 2022 indenture. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 1 and December 1, commencing December 1, 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose the issuance of unsecured senior debt instruments. Intel’s 2023 remarketing of Arizona and Oregon bonds ($423 million) involved general unsecured obligations with specific coupons (3.8% and 4.1%) and maturity dates (2035 and 2040). Similarly, AMD discloses the issuance of $1.0 billion in general unsecured senior notes with defined interest rates (3.924% and 4.393%) and maturity dates (2032 and 2052). Both companies utilize unsecured general obligation structures for long-term financing, though the specific terms, issuers, and amounts differ.

sentences.text: In 2023, we remarketed $423 million aggregate principal amount of bonds issued by the Industrial Development Authority of the City of Chandler, Arizona (the Arizona bonds) and the State of Oregon Business Development Commission (the Oregon bonds).

The bonds are unsecured general obligations in accordance with loan agreements we entered into with each of the Industrial Development Authority of the City of Chandler, Arizona (CIDA) and the State of Oregon Business Development Commission.
The bonds mature in 2035 and 2040 and have 3.8% and 4.1% coupons.
On June 9, 2022, the Company issued $1.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of 3.924% Notes and 4.393% Notes.
The 3.924% Notes and 4.393% Notes are general unsecured senior obligations of the Company.

comparisons.peer_topic: Issuance of Senior Unsecured Notes in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: The company issued senior unsecured notes totaling $10 billion in 2024, with $5 billion issued in July and another $5 billion in October.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose the issuance of significant amounts of unsecured debt. Intel remarketed $423 million of unsecured general obligation bonds in 2023. Broadcom issued $10 billion in senior unsecured notes in 2024 ($5 billion in July and $5 billion in October). While the timing and scale differ, both entities engaged in substantial unsecured debt issuance activities within the disclosed periods, highlighting a shared reliance on unsecured capital markets for funding.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2023 Term Loan Origination for VMware Merger
comparisons.peer_summary: Upon completion of the VMware Merger, the company entered into three unsecured term loan facilities totaling $30,390 million: Term A-2 ($11,195 million), Term A-3 ($11,195 million), and Term A-5 ($8,000 million), under the 2023 Credit Agreement executed on August 15, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose the use of unsecured financing instruments. Intel’s disclosure concerns unsecured general obligation bonds. Broadcom’s disclosure details the entry into three unsecured term loan facilities totaling $30,390 million upon the completion of the VMware Merger. Both filings explicitly characterize these debt instruments as 'unsecured', indicating a similar credit strategy for securing capital without specific collateral backing for these tranches.

comparisons.peer_topic: Seniority and Redemption Terms of Notes
comparisons.peer_summary: All notes are unsecured senior obligations, while subsidiary liabilities are effectively senior to them. Interest is paid semi-annually, and notes may be redeemed prior to maturity subject to a make-whole premium.

NVIDIA explicitly states 'All our notes are unsecured senior obligations.' Both filings confirm the unsecured nature of the debt, establishing a parallel in the security structure of their respective long-term liabilities, although the specific terms and amounts vary.
